messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

Happy New Year! Just a quick reminder that the next bioc-teaching call will take place on Monday, January 11 at 2pm CET. The jitsi link is https://meet.jit.si/BioconductorTeaching. One of the agenda items this time will be to discuss how the group can participate in the newly launched Carpentries lesson development study groups (https://carpentries.org/blog/2020/12/lesson-development-study-groups/).
In addition, we wanted to draw your attention to the fact that the Carpentries is currently running a bonus module on online training for certified Carpentries instructors (see more at https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/instructor-training-bonus-modules/bonus_module_calendar/index.html).

See you on Monday,
Charlotte & Laurent

Hi everyone,

Re-posting for those who might have missed this in a December rush. Please see the message below about the launch of a new program of Lesson Development Study Groups, and read the associated blog post <https://carpentries.org/blog/2020/12/lesson-development-study-groups/> for more details. You still have one week to get your application in!

All the best,

Toby

> On 18. Dec 2020, at 11:40, Toby Hodges <tobyh...@carpentries.org> wrote:
>
>
>
> Hi everyone,
>
>
>
> We are thrilled to announce a new program of Lesson Development Study Groups for members of the Carpentries community who would like develop a new lesson in The Carpentries Incubator <https://github.com/carpentries-incubator/proposals>.
>
>
> The Study Groups program will bring these community members together to develop their lessons as a cohort. Participants will benefit from the process by learning and discussing good practices in lesson design and share their experience as they build their lessons.
>
>
> By the end of the program, participants will have gained practical experience of the backwards design approach to lesson development, written and taught at least one section of their lesson, prepared a plan for the remaining material, and set up a repository to facilitate further collaborative development of their lesson.
>
>
>
> To learn more about the program and how you can apply, please read the blog post announcement <https://carpentries.org/blog/2020/12/lesson-development-study-groups/>, and feel free to contact me (tobyh...@carpentries.org) or reply to this message if you have any questions.
>
>
>
> All the best,
>
>
>
> Toby
